definition: A set of memory optimization techniques for distributed training that eliminates redundant storage of optimizer states, gradients, and parameters across data-parallel workers.
details: ZeRO enables training much larger models than would otherwise fit in available GPU memory by partitioning (rather than replicating) optimizer state, gradients, and parameters across the devices participating in data-parallel training.
story: Imagine teaching a friend to shoot a basketball. They miss, and you walk them backwards through the shot — elbow, wrist, release — to find what needs fixing. Boil it down and it is this: A set of memory optimization techniques for distributed training that eliminates redundant storage of optimizer states, gradients, and parameters across data-parallel workers. Here is why it matters: ZeRO enables training much larger models than would otherwise fit in available GPU memory by partitioning (rather than replicating) optimizer state, gradients, and parameters across the devices participating in data-parallel training. It is learning from every miss instead of repeating the same mistake. That steady, miss-by-miss improvement is ZeRO (Zero Redundancy Optimizer).

citation.title: ZeRO: Memory Optimizations Toward Training Trillion Parameter Models
